subject: Perf architecture deep-dive & load-test gating — scheduling
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@aurora-analytics.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@aurora-analytics.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: performance architecture deep-dive & throughput targets

Hi Mina —

Thanks for the run of the free trial — results look promising. Aurora's platform team would like a technical deep-dive focused on:
- target sustained token throughput for our 750ms SLA (p50/p95/p99) across mix of short/long prompts
- proposed load-test gating criteria before production cutover
- KV cache behavior with our prompt templates and multi-tenant dataset
- fallback policy / canary configuration for model degradations

Could we schedule a 60–90 minute session next week with your performance/serving leads? The people who should join from our side: Priya (platform lead) and an SRE who will run the load tests.

Proposed windows (PST):
- Tue 12/14 10:00–11:30
- Wed 12/15 14:00–15:30

I've attached a short requirements spreadsheet that outlines our peak tokens/sec targets and representative prompt mix (attachment: aurora_requirements.xlsx).

Goal: define a load-test plan and gating checklist we can run end-to-end within Aurora's staging environment, then iterate on config tuning.

Thanks — looking forward to your availability.

— Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, Aurora Analytics
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@aurora-analytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 09:50:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: performance architecture deep-dive & throughput targets

Hi Alex —

Really appreciate the clear brief and the spreadsheet — that's exactly what helps us scope the run. We can run a 75-minute technical deep-dive that covers architecture (serving runtime and routing), load-test plan, and a short gating checklist. Suggested agenda:

1) 10m introductions & goals
2) 20m runtime/serving architecture (Marcus + Karthik)
3) 25m load-test plan & token distribution (I will walk through the proposed test cases)
4) 15m gating checklist, rollback/fallback, next steps
5) buffer / Q&A

Attendees from Redwood: Marcus (serving runtime), Karthik (load-test config & compilation/kernel notes), Laura (observability & query-level tracing), and me to coordinate the gating decisions.

From your proposed windows, we can do Tue 12/14 10:00–11:15 PST but Marcus has a conflict the morning of 12/14 that I only just discovered — can you do a hard hold on Tue 12/14 10:00–11:15 and, if needed, Wed 12/15 14:00–15:15 PST as backup? If you confirm Tue as primary I will:
- upload a Redwood-side load-test outline (redwood-loadtest-outline.xlsx) to the shared drive
- list required credentials / ephemeral endpoints we need from your SRE
- include pre-reads (token distributions + sample prompts) 48 hours before the session

Also: can you confirm whether Aurora will run the load generator from within your cloud project or would you like Redwood to run an external generator? That affects KV cache priming guidance.

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: performance architecture deep-dive & throughput targets

Mina — quick note: I have a customer QBR that conflicts with 12/14 10:00–11:15 PST. I can do 12/15 14:00–15:30 PST without trouble. If we have to keep 12/14 (Alex prefers it), we could split the session — Karthik and I can prerecord a 15–20m runbook walkthrough and send it as a pre-read, then join live for the gating discussion.

Action items if we move to 12/15 14:00:
- Karthik: update load-test spreadsheet with kernel/quantization options we plan to try (owner: karthik_iyer)
- Mina: publish agenda + upload redwood-loadtest-outline.xlsx to shared drive (owner: mina_haddad)
- Laura: prepare a short dashboard snapshot showing token-level cost and p99 latency breakouts (owner: laura_bennett)
- Evelyn: confirm we have a spare GPU slot on the dedicated pool for an isolated run (owner: evelyn_hart)

Karthik — can you confirm ETA on the spreadsheet updates?

> 
> Really appreciate the clear brief and the spreadsheet — that's exactly what helps us scope the run. We can run a 75-minute technical deep-dive...

— Marcus

To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: performance architecture deep-dive & throughput targets

Thanks everyone — Wed 12/15 14:00–15:30 PST works for us. Appreciate the flexibility, Marcus.

Please include the following for the session:
- shared calendar invite (I've accepted the provisional hold) — https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=aurora-redwood-perf-deepdive-20261210
- shared drive with both attachments so our SRE can prep — https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cREDWOOD-AURORA-loadtest
- confirm whether Redwood will provide an external load generator VM or we should provision within Aurora (we prefer to run in our staging project if possible)

I've attached our original spreadsheet again (aurora_requirements.xlsx). We'll add our SRE contact to the calendar. Looking forward to the walkthrough and the checklist; after the session we'll schedule a 2–3 hour run for the gate test.

— Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, Aurora Analytics
